summary: Test-writing (red) phase for issue #5: committed compile-guarded tests that specify the generated OpenAPI client (module GeneratedAPIClient, six operations, stubbed ClientTransport responses) plus wire-contract tests pinning the migration; LID doc maps every acceptance criterion to its verification and pre-records prose-contract deltas and endpoint gaps. Swift toolchain is unavailable in this Linux container, so tests could not be executed locally; CI on macOS runs swift test. Implementation deliverables remain pending the implementation run.

verification.reason: Adding swift-openapi-generator/runtime and vendoring the spec are implementation-phase actions (not permitted in this tests-only run). The canImport(GeneratedAPIClient) guard plus the failing fallback test demonstrate the module is missing today and activate the full suite once generated.
Six-operation coverage (manifest, recent sheets, create capture, measurements, judgments, ranked results) is specified test-first behind the compile guard; the generated client does not exist yet.

Model replacement is implementation work. Wire-contract tests pin the behavior the rewrite must preserve (paths, bearer header, absolute-URL manifest fetch) and are committed green-by-design against the current client.

Tests exist and use only in-process stubs (ClientTransport / URLProtocol), but no Swift toolchain exists in this Linux container, so they could not be executed locally; CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, macOS) runs swift test.
PR description is authored at implementation time; deltas and gaps are pre-recorded in the LID doc for verbatim reuse, pending reconciliation with the published viamin/color_matching#110 spec.
swift test --disable-sandbox green requires the generated client to exist (implementation run) and a Swift toolchain (absent in this container).
Same as AC-5: PR body is produced when the PR is opened in the implementation run.
